### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/http-conformance`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/package.json`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/qa/http-conformance/vitest.config.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND (literal, a string literal in unmatched))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/* (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/comments (route, a path literal in a comment in ICommentDoorsService; a path literal in a comment on a changed line), /api/v1/comments/:id (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line), /api/v1/comments/:id/resolution (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line), /api/v1/comments/reactions/:id (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line), /comments/:id (route, a path literal in COMMENT_DOOR_PATHS; a path literal in ROUTE_LEDGER; a path literal in a comment on a changed line), /comments/:id/resolution (route, a path literal in COMMENT_DOOR_PATHS; a path literal in ROUTE_LEDGER; a path literal in a comment on a changed line), /comments/reactions/:id (route, a path literal in COMMENT_DOOR_PATHS; a path literal in ROUTE_LEDGER; a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND (literal, a string literal in unmatched))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/comments (route, a path literal in a comment in ICommentDoorsService; a path literal in a comment on a changed line), /api/v1/comments/reactions/:id (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line), /comments/reactions/:id (route, a path literal in COMMENT_DOOR_PATHS; a path literal in ROUTE_LEDGER; a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-5.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/package.json`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/qa/http-conformance/vitest.config.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/api/v1 (route, 128 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 77517533d3b8fd8aafb2f4203ba384e31c3ae7cf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bf47c34cdf2f4943602c61c219d58600031229cb` — the merge of head `e7dcb26cc49a8cb61a3cddb0104b0371e7ffb7a8` into base `77517533d3b8fd8aafb2f4203ba384e31c3ae7cf`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bf47c34cdf2f4943602c61c219d58600031229cb && git checkout bf47c34cdf2f4943602c61c219d58600031229cb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 77517533d3b8fd8aafb2f4203ba384e31c3ae7cf e7dcb26cc49a8cb61a3cddb0104b0371e7ffb7a8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 77517533d3b8fd8aafb2f4203ba384e31c3ae7cf && git merge --no-ff e7dcb26cc49a8cb61a3cddb0104b0371e7ffb7a8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 77517533d3b8fd8aafb2f4203ba384e31c3ae7cf
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 77517533d3b8fd8aafb2f4203ba384e31c3ae7cf` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6b916dcfcb9f31150b539ef9cc22497516689f28`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/comment-doors-service.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/core-service-contracts.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/index.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-doors-member.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/comments.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts

Check-runs on this head when read (66): 20 success, 9 skipped, 37 still in progress, 0 failed. Green and relevant: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Validate Package Dependencies, Spec property liveness, Type Check source gates, Type Check debt ledger, Lint ESLint, Lint docs and code guards, Lint repo and tooling gates, Lint scoped tooling self-tests, Dogfood Regression Gate. Pending, so no verdict yet: Build Core, Test Core 1 to 10, Type Check workspace, Type Check consumer gates, Lint scoped slot lookup and corpus, Lint scoped query-options erasure, Lint PM dispatch-gates, Lint CI release and engine gates, and the UI jobs. This record stands only if those conclude green.

### ① Derived judgments

- New export `ICommentDoorsService` from `@objectstack/spec/contracts`, one optional member `handleCommentDoor(request: Request)` answering a promised `Response`. Right. `index.ts` re-exports the one module, and `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` each gain exactly that one row. Nothing else is published.
- New key `comments` on `ServiceSlotContracts`. Right. The typed lookup for `comments` moves from `unknown` to the contract. No reader on `main` resolves a `comments` service, and none registers one (searched `registerService` / `getService` / `resolveService` over `packages` on `origin/main`: 0 hits). The discovery flag `comments: { enabled }` in `http-dispatcher.ts` is derived from the `sys_comment` object, not from a service slot, so it does not collide.
- Derived and unstated: the slot name is now taken at runtime. `AuditPlugin.init()` registers `comments` unconditionally, and `plugin-loader.ts` throws `Service 'comments' already registered` on a second registration. A third-party composition that already owns a `comments` service would fail to boot with AuditPlugin. Nothing in this repo does; acceptable, and worth one line in the changeset.
- Accept-set on the wire: three method and path shapes that answered a 404 through the dispatcher now answer through the member, on both the plain and the environment-scoped spelling. Every other `PUT` / `DELETE` under `/comments` still answers `deps.routeNotFound`, which is bound to the dispatcher's own fallback `this.routeNotFound`, so nothing that answered before answers differently. `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH` are not claimed. Right.
- "Nothing narrows" holds. No export, key, accepted value or route is removed, and the auth-gate allow-list and the membership skip list are untouched (`packages/core` has no hunk; `enforceProjectMembership` has no hunk).
- Shape against the precedents on `main`: same signature, same optionality, same per-request slot read, same 501 pair, same body-unread forward and same sanitised 500 as `IWebhookService.handleRedeliver` and `domains/webhooks.ts`. Two deliberate differences, both right: one member for three routes (so the claim is a `segment` claim narrowed in the handler instead of an `exact` one), and a URL rewrite to the wire path, which the single-route precedent did not need.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in both the PR body and the changeset. This matches AGENTS.md: a service contract is not something a metadata author writes, so the kind is `none`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. Check Changeset is green. The declaration is the lane's; the widening it names is right and complete as far as the diff publishes.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — as declared by the lane; judged right and complete.

The changeset body does not mention that `@objectstack/plugin-audit` gains a production dependency on `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` (see N1). Not a level question.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions` (report 7083912355): one entry, the verify-lock slot behaviour, recommendation A (seat notes it, no action on this PR). Answered: it is tooling, outside this contract, and nothing in the diff depends on it.
- Ruling fit, escalated for the maintainer's information, not blocking. Ruling 6079645593 rules A plus the sweep: each member of the class "is bridged the same way", and the sweep report "names any further member". This PR is that shape. But the same ruling records the class as three producers, "not a wide one", from a census of `getRawApp()` mounts. The comment doors are a fourth producer, mounted through `IHttpServer` verbs, and the dev names two more families (personal-views, attachments). The seat applied A by extension (7081381198) without a new word from the maintainer. The shape is sound; the maintainer should know the class is now measured wider, because the ruling parked the conformance pin A-3 "until the sweep report re-raises it with the measured class".
- Hosted acceptance is not evidenced, escalated to the seat. The card's acceptance is a hosted environment (local cloud rig or staging). The PR's proof is `createHonoApp` over one kernel with no `http.server`. The card's measured body does not match the path this PR bridges (S1 below). `Fixes #36469` will close the card at merge, before any hosted reading and before a cloud pin carries this head. The card should stay open, or its acceptance move to the cloud pin card, as #22438 did with cloud#2549.
- Identity on the hosted path, flagged. The member resolves the caller with the tenant kernel's own `auth` service (`ctx.getService('auth')`), while the dispatcher's own identity step falls back to the host kernel (`resolveService` chain). If a hosted tenant kernel carries no `auth` service of its own, every door answers 401 after the dispatcher admitted the caller. The webhooks precedent makes the same assumption, and cloud is not readable from here, so this is unmeasured, not a finding.
- Who can do what (brief item e): no hunk changes it. `registerCommentDoors` is the old inline body moved verbatim: the same `optional` helper, the same `getEngine`, the same `platformCallerResolver` sources, the same two registrars with the same deps. The member runs those registrars, so the unreact door (own row by `created_by`), the resolution door (read as the caller, then the posting gate) and the own-comment delete door (own row by `author_id`, refused under replies) decide exactly as the mount does. The member cannot be reached around its own caller resolution: any caller of `handleCommentDoor` still passes steps 1 to 3 of each door. Through the dispatcher the ADR-0069 gate and the membership gate run first, so the hosted door is stricter, never looser.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; the engine calls are the unchanged registrars'.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/comment-doors-service.ts`. Read sentence by sentence against the registrars on `main` (`comment-reaction-routes.ts`, `comment-routes.ts`, `core/src/security/own-row-delete-routes.ts`) and the member. True: caller from the request's credentials through the kernel's `auth` service; 401 with no caller; 403 for a held sign-in; the envelope; `{ id, deleted: true }` and `{ id, is_resolved, resolved_by, resolved_at }`; 404 `ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND` for a request outside the three routes (the member pre-matches and answers it itself); the wire path requirement (the domain rewrites to it); no `ExecutionContext`; one caller; not allow-listed and not skipped; 501 for an empty slot or absent member. The contract holds against ruling A and against its first consumer. One sentence names the wrong miss code (S1).

`packages/spec/src/contracts/core-service-contracts.ts`. The `comments` entry states the registration and the probe correctly. Holds.

`packages/spec/src/contracts/index.ts`. One `export *` of a module with one export. Holds.

`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts`. The extraction is equivalent to the old body, and the mount on `http.server` calls it once; the member builds its own table, so nothing is mounted twice on a socket. The no-server branch moves from `warn` to `info` and still contains the words `comment doors mounted`, which the card's log acceptance reads. Holds.

`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-doors-member.ts`. The private `HonoHttpServer` never listens; its constructor installs only the error envelope, compression, session-read isolation, body limit and noindex seams, and the route wrapper opens a fresh session-read scope, so a request served in process does not reach the outer request's session reads. The lazy build is synchronous, so two first requests cannot build two tables. Tried: a path the pre-match admits but Hono does not route (none found; both treat `:id` as one non-empty segment), an empty id, a doubled slash, `reactions` as an id (same answer as the mount). Holds, with N1 to N4.

`packages/runtime/src/domains/comments.ts`. Exactly three shapes are claimed. The trailing-slash spelling and the scoped spelling are both rewritten to the wire path, with headers, signal, query string and the unread body stream carried over; the request is handed on as it is when the path already matches. The handler never reads `req.body`, so the adapter's refusal-on-read never pre-empts the door. The slot is read per request on the request kernel first. Both 501 legs and both 500 legs are as documented. No header or credential is dropped in the forward. Holds, with S1.

`packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts`. One import and one registration, after the webhooks domain; no later domain claims `/comments`, and both preamble gates run before the registry lookup. Holds.

`packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts`. Three `server-only` rows; the notes agree with the domain. The census number is the tool's. Holds, with S1 on the miss code it names.

S1 (should-fix) — The account of the defect does not agree with the tree, and it is written into the contract and both implementing modules. `comments.ts` says that on the hosted shape the three doors "answered the host's unmatched `404 ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND`"; `comment-doors-member.ts` says "the host's catch-all answered ... with the unmatched `404 ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND`"; the spec jsdoc and the ledger rows promise the absence answer is "never `ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND`". On `origin/main`, `createHonoApp`'s `${prefix}/*` catch-all is terminal and always calls `dispatch()` (`packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts`), and `dispatch()` answers an unclaimed path with `routeNotFound`, that is `404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` carrying `route`. Neither the adapter nor the dispatcher can produce `ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND`: its only producer on this path is `HonoHttpServer.unmatchedResponse`, the answer of a host that listens through `plugin-hono-server` with `DispatcherPlugin`'s explicit mounts, which has no catch-all (`dispatcher-plugin.ts`: "there is no catch-all"). The same module contradicts itself: it says the other `/comments` shapes keep `404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`, "exactly what it answered before this domain existed", which was equally true of the three doors. The PR's own red state confirms it: with the domain removed the unit test reads `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`, and the conformance assertion `not.toContain('ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND')` was already true before the change on that shape. Why it matters beyond wording: the card measured `ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND "Not found"` on the hosted rig, so the request it measured was answered by a layer this diff does not touch, or the rig is not the `createHonoApp` shape. A host composed without the catch-all does not reach the new domain at all, and this diff adds no mount in `dispatcher-plugin.ts`. The dev's first report called the body "exactly the card's body" from reading, with the runtime leg NOT MEASURED. Fix: state the prior answer as the tree gives it (the dispatcher's `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`), make the absence promise "never `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`" as both precedents do (or name both codes), and say in the PR which host layer produced the card's body, or that it is unexplained. The hosted reading itself is the acceptance flag in ③.

N1 (nit) — `@objectstack/plugin-audit` takes a production dependency on `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` and imports `HonoHttpServer` statically. On `main` no domain plugin does: plugin-auth, service-datasource, runtime and rest carry it as a dev dependency only, and the precedent members (plugin-webhooks) serve their door without a transport. Every kernel that composes AuditPlugin now loads `hono`, `@hono/node-server` and `node:https` at import. The private table also has its own body limit (the default or `OS_HTTP_MAX_BODY_BYTES`, not the host's `setMaxRequestBodyBytes`) and its own logger. The trade is deliberate (one request builder, so the two faces cannot drift) and no gate objects; record it as an accepted deviation, because the personal-views and attachments members will copy it.

N2 (nit) — The peer address does not survive the forward. The own-row caller resolver passes `transport.remoteAddress` for the `credential_use` row an admitted API key writes; in the private table `fetch(request)` carries no socket, so the hosted door writes that row without an address. No verdict reads it (`request-execution-context.ts`: "Never read for any verdict"), and a `Request`-only member cannot carry it. Follow-up for the class, not this PR.

N3 (nit) — `comment-doors-member.ts` calls its 404 "the transport's own unmatched answer". For a door path with another verb the transport answers `405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` with `Allow`; the member answers 404, as the contract says. The dispatcher never forwards such a request, so it is unreachable from the one caller.

N4 (nit) — The three shapes are written twice (`COMMENT_DOOR_ROUTES` in plugin-audit, `COMMENT_DOOR_PATHS` in runtime). The member's doc says `matchCommentDoor` is exported "so the runtime's claim and this member can be pinned to the same three shapes", and nothing at this head references either list outside its own file. Drift fails closed (a 404 on either side), and the conformance suite drives all three doors end to end.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-36469-comment-doors-hosted`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmT4eA4YqtxfiPyLPih`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e7dcb26cc49a8cb61a3cddb0104b0371e7ffb7a8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/comment-doors-service.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/core-service-contracts.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/index.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-doors-member.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/comments.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts

Delta round on the at-tier record 7084078045 (head `6b916dcfcb9f31150b539ef9cc22497516689f28`). Everything that record judged and this round does not name stands as written there.

Check-runs on this head when read (74): all completed, none failed; 63 success and 11 skipped by reading the list. The runs that were pending on the previous head are now green here: Build Core, Test Core 1 to 10 and its roll-up, Type Check workspace, Type Check consumer gates, Type Check source gates, Type Check debt ledger, Lint ESLint (the parse error at `604b45ec` is gone), Lint scoped slot lookup and corpus, Lint scoped query-options erasure, Lint PM dispatch-gates, Lint CI release and engine gates, Lint docs and code guards, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Validate Package Dependencies, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, and the UI jobs. The skipped ones are opt-in or queue-only jobs (merge-queue dogfood shards, Temporal Conformance, packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness, queue verdicts).

What this head is: `acc0d0cd` is a merge of the previous head `6b916dcf` with main at `f3a8a13c` (its two parents), followed by two commits, `604b45ec` and `e7dcb26c`. `git diff acc0d0cd e7dcb26c` is the rework alone: six files, text plus one added test assertion (the changeset, `comment-doors-member.ts`, the conformance test, `comments.ts`, `route-ledger.ts`, `comment-doors-service.ts`). Main's carry-over touches one Scope file, `audit-plugin.ts`, in one hunk: the order of `installActivitySummaryLocale` and `installActivityFieldRedaction` (#36290). It is not a comment-door hunk, and the net diff of that file against `f3a8a13c` still shows only the door hunks, so no judgment changes. Main has no change between `f3a8a13c` and the local `origin/main` under `packages/spec/src/contracts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit`, `packages/runtime/src`, `packages/adapters/hono/src` or `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src`. The dev report and the PR body say main was merged "at `c57ade2f5a`"; no such object exists in this checkout, and the merge's main-side parent is `f3a8a13c`. That is a claim I could not match, not a tree fact.

### ① Derived judgments

- The rework publishes nothing new. `ICommentDoorsService`, its one optional member and the `comments` key on `ServiceSlotContracts` are byte-identical to the previous head except three jsdoc lines on the absence promise. Right.
- The absence promise changed wording, not behaviour: an empty slot or an absent member still answers `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` on both legs of `handleCommentsRequest`. The jsdoc now names the code the dispatcher would otherwise give (`404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`) and keeps the transport's (`404 ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND`) beside it. Right, and it now matches the two precedents on `main`.
- Accept-set on the wire: unchanged from the previous head. No route, verb, export or slot key is added or removed by the rework.
- The conformance pin gained `not.toContain('ROUTE_NOT_FOUND')` beside the existing `ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND` and status-not-404 assertions. That is the assertion that was red before the domain existed on this shape; the previous record noted the old one was already true before the change. A test file, so the lane's, but it is what makes the first pin mean what its title says.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/plugin-audit`; the rework edits the changeset's prose below the front matter only. Check Changeset is green on this head. The changeset now also states the `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` runtime dependency and that the `comments` service name is taken (a second registration fails boot with a duplicate-service error), which is what ① of the previous record asked to be said.

### ③ Boundary flags
